_comment.schema: <kernel>: { <case_id>: {sizes: [...], dtype?: str, lnc?: int, rtol?: float, atol?: float} }
_comment.sizes: Required. Integers in the spec's dim_vars order (the same order --sizes binds positionally).
_comment.dtype: Optional. Passed through as --dtype. Omit to use the spec's make_inputs default. Only present where a case differs from that default (e.g. a same-shape dtype twin).
_comment.lnc: Optional. 2 opts the case into the lnc=2 sharding search (search + emit + bench each codegen-emittable sharding head-to-head against the lnc=1 winner). Absent => lnc=1, today's single-core path.
_comment.rtol_atol: Optional. PRESENCE of rtol/atol marks a head-to-head case: it gets a generated per-case nkilib harness (out/winners/<stem>_case.py). A bench-only case omits them. Adding a head-to-head case also requires the spec's baseline_op + torch_ref.
_comment.readers: Skip any key beginning with '_' (this comment) at both the kernel and case levels.

_attention_nkilib_tolerance: atol/rtol are 5e-2 (not the 2e-2 the other attention cases use) because bf16 exp error, not codegen, dominates the check: the softmax has no row-max subtraction, so the emitted kernel simulates to ~1e-6 against the fp32 reference and the gap is intrinsic bf16-vs-fp32 precision. Cases run at d=128, nkilib attention_cte's mainstream head dim (Llama3-70B / Qwen3 / Gemma3 configs use d=64/128), unscaled (softmax_scale=1.0), which puts max(q @ k_t) at ~44, safely under the fp32 exp limit of 88.72. At d=128 num_d_tiles=1, so attention_cte's flash threshold stays at 10240 and the hand side runs full-scores (non-flash) through s=8192, the same algorithm the Axon kernel uses, so the comparison is apples-to-apples on both count and algorithm. d=512 was retired: it is the kernel's max head dim (Gemma4-global only) and its flash threshold collapses to 10240/num_d_tiles=2560, so the hand side switched to sectioned flash at s>=4k while Axon stayed full-scores, an apples-to-oranges comparison.

linear_attention._note: Cross-attention linear attention out = Q(KᵀV); dim order sq, sk, dk, dv. Distinct sq/sk and dk/dv keep the four schedule roles distinct (m=sq, n=dv, p=dk, k=sk). Bare matmul→matmul chain (no combine between the matmuls). dv (the n/wide role) is 512 (= tile_n) so it tiles without the wide clamp; dv<512 is a known tiling-resolution gap for this dim structure (the wide role's raw dim has no derivable extent, so _resolve_tiles skips it).
